Her hair is naturally red, worn at times in long braids or flowing unbraided in a torrent of brightness, though friends sometimes refer to it as auburn. Her hair has also been cut short into silky curls after being closely shingled, and it was briefly green during one incident.

label: Personality
value: Anne Shirley is a passionate individual.
unit: A passionate, imaginative, and serious-minded individual, she possesses a strong will, deep personal loyalty, and a keen romantic nature. Though smart, obedient, and quick to learn, her heedless and impulsive temperament often leads her to fall into daydreams mid-task. She experiences intense emotional shifts, frequently flying high on the wings of anticipation before crashing down into despair. Academically ambitious, her motivations include excelling in her studies to win a scholarship, making a proud impression, and ultimately attending college to become a teacher. She also aspires to emulate those she admires and strives to add beauty to the world around her. Creatively skilled in storytelling, singing, and interacting with children, she nevertheless harbors a distinct fear of entering the Haunted Wood after dark.

label: History
value: Anne Shirley was taken in as an orphan by Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert at Green Gables.
unit: Anne Shirley was taken in as an orphan by Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert at Green Gables, where she quickly formed a lifelong friendship with Diana Barry and began attending the local school. After Gilbert Blythe teased her about her hair, she smashed her slate over his head and refused to speak to him, though she later forgave him in secret during their intense academic rivalry. Anne continued to reside in Avonlea for six years, during which she frequently engaged in imaginative misadventures, such as inventing ghosts in the Haunted Wood with Diana and mistakenly serving her friend currant wine. Over the years, Matthew bought her a long-desired dress with puffed sleeves for a concert, and Anne eventually earned top honors on the Queen's Entrance examination. When Matthew suddenly passed away and Marilla faced potential blindness, Anne chose to forfeit her college scholarship to remain at Green Gables, leading Gilbert to give up the local teaching post so she could take it. As the village schoolteacher, she organized the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, accidentally sold her neighbor Mr. Harrison's cow before making amends, and helped Marilla raise two young twins, Davy and Dora. Through her teaching and social calls, she befriended local figures such as Miss Lavendar Lewis and eventually reconnected Miss Lavendar with her former suitor, Stephen Irving. Years after their initial schoolroom clash, Anne permanently ended her feud with Gilbert Blythe, coming to regard him as a close friend while preparing for her ultimate departure to Redmond College.

Anne continued to reside in Avonlea for six years, during which she frequently engaged in imaginative misadventures, such as inventing ghosts in the Haunted Wood with Diana and mistakenly serving her friend currant wine. label: Quote

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I love pretty things; and I hate to look in the glass and see something that isn’t pretty. It makes me feel so sorrowful—just as I feel when I look at any ugly thing. I pity it because it isn’t beautiful."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I love Green Gables already, and I never loved any place before. No place ever seemed like home. Oh, Marilla, I’m so happy. I could pray right now and not find it a bit hard."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "Oh, Marilla, I’m frightened—now that it has come I’m actually frightened. What if she shouldn’t like me! It would be the most tragical disappointment of my life."

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "But I’m sure I shan’t sleep a blessed wink, Miss Shirley, ma’am, for fear that something’ll go wrong at the last minute . . . the cream won’t whip . . . or Mr. Irving’ll have a stroke and not be able to come."

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "but there’s so much to do yet . . . and oh, Miss Shirley, ma’am, I’m skeered it’s going to rain and I wish you’d get up and tell me you think it ain’t."

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "it’s plain to be seen you and Miss Lavendar have got a secret and I think, begging your pardon if I’m too forward, Miss Shirley, ma’am, that it’s real mean not to tell me when we’ve all been such chums."

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "Yes, ma’am. Come in, ma’am. I’ll tell Miss Lavendar you’re here, ma’am. She’s upstairs, ma’am."

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "and they’re married safe and sound, no matter what happens now. The bags of rice are in the pantry, ma’am, and the old shoes are behind the door, and the cream for whipping is on the sullar steps."

label: Lavendar Lewis
value: Charlotta serves Miss Lavendar Lewis.
unit: Charlotta serves as the young helper and handmaiden to Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge. She assists Miss Lavendar with hosting guests for imaginary tea parties, setting the table, and demonstrating the lodge's unique echoes. Charlotta shows deep concern for her mistress's emotional well-being, confiding in Anne when Miss Lavendar suffers from unusual despondency and apathy. After helping prepare for Miss Lavendar's eventual wedding, Charlotta works alongside Anne to tidy up Echo Lodge following the ceremony.

label: History
value: Davy Keith lost his father as an infant.
unit: Davy Keith lost his father as an infant and was raised without proper guidance until Marilla Cuthbert brought him and his twin sister, Dora, to live at Green Gables. Displaying an unruly and mischievous nature, he quickly caused trouble by playing pranks, stealing jam, and locking Dora in a toolhouse. After his lies made Anne Shirley cry, Davy tearfully resolved to stop lying, and Anne and Marilla committed to guiding him despite his misbehavior. Over time, Davy questioned Anne on various topics such as prayer and heaven, accidentally ruined a batch of lemon pies meant for a guest, and contended with feelings of jealousy toward Anne's student Paul Irving. His permanent stay at Green Gables was secured after Richard Keith passed away, leaving a fund set aside for the twins' care. Although he continued to require redirection at the dinner table, Davy grew deeply attached to Anne, warmly expressing his affection for her when she tucked him into bed.

value: Davy Keith said: “Why?” queried Davy, settling comfortably down and looking up with a tearstained, investigating face. “Why ain’t whopper as good as falsehood? I want to know. It’s just as big a word.”

label: History
value: Diana Barry was named by a schoolmaster who boarded with her family when she was born.
unit: Named by a schoolmaster who boarded with her family when she was born, Diana Barry lived at Orchard Slope when she first met Anne Shirley. The two quickly formed a deep friendship and pledged to be bosom friends forever. Their bond faced an early trial when Mrs. Barry temporarily forbade Diana from playing with Anne, but they were allowed to resume their friendship after Anne saved Diana's sister Minnie May from severe croup. Diana remained Anne's constant companion through their school years, joining her in forming a story club and sharing secret notes. When Anne tied for first place on the island in her entrance examinations, Diana rushed to Green Gables with the newspaper to deliver the news. Together, they canvassed for the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, took woodland walks to hidden places like Hester Gray's garden and Echo Lodge, and navigated local mishaps. Though distress settled over Diana when Anne prepared to leave Avonlea for Redmond College, she assured Anne of her steadfast affection. Shortly before assisting with Miss Lavendar's garden wedding, Diana got engaged to Fred Wright.

value: Diana Barry said: "I’m awfully glad you’ve come to live at Green Gables. It will be jolly to have somebody to play with. There isn’t any other girl who lives near enough to play with, and I’ve no sisters big enough."

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: "Why, he makes fun of all the girls. He laughs at mine because it’s so black. He’s called me a crow a dozen times; and I never heard him apologize for anything before, either."

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: "I do think you’re mean. What shall I do? Mr. Phillips will make me sit with that horrid Gertie Pye—I know he will because she is sitting alone. Do come back, Anne."

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: “I don’t believe he’ll find the doctor at Carmody,” sobbed Diana. “I know that Dr. Blair went to town and I guess Dr. Spencer would go too. Young Mary Joe never saw anybody with croup and Mrs. Lynde is away. Oh, Anne!”

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: "I guess we must have made as much as ten dollars. Mind you, Mr. Allan is going to send an account of it to the Charlottetown papers."

An industrious child, she finds joy in helping with small tasks, tending to her work in a careful, systematic, and dispassionate manner.

label: History
value: Dora Keith was brought to live at Green Gables.
unit: Dora Keith was brought to live at Green Gables alongside her twin brother Davy, though early on she suffered from his mischief when he caused her to fall into a pigpen and later locked her in a toolhouse. Unlike her unruly brother, Dora was noted for her quiet perfection. She was frightened at school by a classmate's ghost stories, but her future at Green Gables was eventually secured when her relative Richard Keith passed away and left trust money allowing her and Davy to stay permanently.

label: History
value: Gilbert Blythe spent three years in Alberta with his sick father.
unit: Gilbert Blythe spent three years in Alberta with his sick father and spent a summer visiting cousins in New Brunswick before returning home. Upon his return to school, he teased Anne Shirley by pulling her braid and calling her 'Carrots,' causing her to smash a slate over his head and angrily refuse his apology. Although Anne maintained a fierce academic rivalry with him over the following years, Gilbert rescued her when she was stranded on a bridge pile, though she again rejected his offer of friendship. Later, Gilbert won the medal at Queen's Academy while Anne won the Avery Scholarship. Upon learning that Anne planned to give up her scholarship to remain in Avonlea with Marilla, Gilbert gave up his position as the Avonlea school teacher so Anne could have it, leading Anne to finally end their feud and become close friends. As a teacher himself, Gilbert discussed teaching methods and creative pursuits with Anne and joined her in various local matters, including the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. He remained a constant companion and friend to Anne, spending time with her in conversation after village events and shared experiences.

As a teacher himself, Gilbert discussed teaching methods and creative pursuits with Anne and joined her in various local matters, including the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. He remained a constant companion and friend to Anne, spending time with her in conversation after village events and shared experiences.

value: Gilbert Blythe said: "We were born to be good friends, Anne. You’ve thwarted destiny enough. I know we can help each other in many ways. You are going to keep up your studies, aren’t you? So am I. Come, I’m going to walk home with you."

label: Personality
value: Jane Andrews is a steady person.
unit: Jane Andrews is a steady, sensible, and lady-like person who remains unflappable regardless of the situation. Known for her plain, plodding, and conscientious nature, she takes a practical and strict approach to her responsibilities, even punishing her pupils when they make funny speeches. Her ambitions have included studying for the Entrance examination to Queen's, excelling in domestic science where she carried off top honors, and devoting her life to teaching without marrying. As a teacher, her primary aims are to earn her salary fairly, please the trustees, and achieve a place on the School Inspector's roll of honor.

label: History
value: Jane Andrews grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Jane Andrews grew up in Avonlea as a close friend of Anne Shirley. She traveled with Anne, Diana, and her brother Billy to the White Sands Hotel for a benefit concert, after which the girls reflected together on wealth and contentment during the drive home. Jane later attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne and their peers, occasionally visiting Anne at her boarding house to help ease her homesickness. As she prepared to begin teaching, Jane joined Anne and Gilbert Blythe in a discussion about classroom discipline and teaching methods. She remained active in community life, joining her friends to lament a paint mix-up at the town hall, participating in a woodland picnic outing to Hester Gray's garden, and serving alongside Anne and Diana on a Village Improvement Society committee that successfully pressured Judson Parker to cancel his fence advertisements.

label: History
value: Miss Lavendar Lewis was named by her father.
unit: Named by her father after his favorite scent, Miss Lavendar Lewis suffered a broken heart when a youthful romantic quarrel led her former fiancé, Stephen Irving, to leave her. Years later, living at Echo Lodge with her young helper Charlotta, she invited lost visitors Anne Shirley and Diana Barry to an imaginary tea party, where she inquired about Stephen's son after Anne inadvertently mentioned him. Following a visit where she shared the story of her past romance with Anne, Miss Lavendar was introduced to Stephen's son, Paul, and formed an immediate, fond friendship with him. After experiencing a period of despondency, she received a note from the returning Stephen via Anne and reconciled with him during an evening visit at Echo Lodge. The two were subsequently married in an intimate ceremony in her garden before departing together.

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "But oh, won’t you stay and have tea with me? Please, do. Mr. Kimball’s will have tea over before you get there. And Charlotta the Fourth and I will be so glad to have you."

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "to believe I’m old. Now, who are you . . . just for convenience’ sake? Diana Barry? And Anne Shirley? May I pretend that I’ve known you for a hundred years and call you Anne and Diana right away?"

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "I love them myself. They are very good company . . . with a little pretending. On calm evenings Charlotta the Fourth and I often sit out here and amuse ourselves with them. Charlotta, take back the horn and hang it carefully in its place."

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "It gave me a shock to hear about Stephen’s son that first day you were here, Anne. I’ve never been able to mention him to you since, but I’ve wanted to know all about him. What sort of a boy is he?"

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "Oh, I’m not so old as I thought . . . and I don’t need a single blue pill! Girls, when you come back with your strawberries we’ll have tea out here under the silver poplar. I’ll have it all ready for you with home-grown cream."

label: Personality
value: Marilla Cuthbert is a sensible woman.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert is a sensible, self-contained, and practical woman who disdains imaginative notions, preferring to maintain neatness and apple-pie order. Driven by a rigid conscience and a stern devotion to duty, she aims to drill Anne into a tranquil uniformity of disposition. She is strict, critical, and fond of attaching morals to her remarks to children, while also refusing on principle to criticize ministers. Though she can be inexorable, unsympathetic, and slightly grim or sarcastic—especially when suffering from headaches—she is also noted for having mellowed. Additionally, she is cautious and deliberate in her decision-making, deeply stoic about concealing excitement, and celebrated for her skill in making three-year-old homemade currant wine.

unit: Marilla Cuthbert is a sensible, self-contained, and practical woman who disdains imaginative notions, preferring to maintain neatness and apple-pie order. Driven by a rigid conscience and a stern devotion to duty, she aims to drill Anne into a tranquil uniformity of disposition. She is strict, critical, and fond of attaching morals to her remarks to children, while also refusing on principle to criticize ministers. Though she can be inexorable, unsympathetic, and slightly grim or sarcastic—especially when suffering from headaches—she is also noted for having mellowed. Additionally, she is cautious and deliberate in her decision-making, deeply stoic about concealing excitement, and celebrated for her skill in making three-year-old homemade currant wine.

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert grew up at Green Gables.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert grew up at Green Gables, having lived there for sixty years after being raised under traditional childhood discipline. In her youth, she quarreled with John Blythe and refused to forgive him when he asked, a decision she later recounted to Anne Shirley after adopting her. When Marilla and her brother Matthew decided to adopt an orphan boy to help on the farm, a mix-up resulted in Anne arriving at Green Gables instead. Though initially shocked and determined to send the girl back, Marilla took pity on Anne after hearing of her hard childhood during a drive to White Sands. Deciding to let her stay, Marilla resolved to raise and educate Anne properly. Over time, Marilla grew deeply affectionate toward Anne, caring for her through various childhood misadventures, such as when Anne mistakenly dyed her hair green and Marilla had to cut it off. When Matthew died suddenly of a heart attack following a bank failure, Marilla and Anne comforted each other in their shared grief. Shortly after, an oculist informed Marilla that she faced total blindness if she did not give up heavy eye work, threatening her ability to keep Green Gables. To prevent this, Anne forfeited her college scholarship to stay home, teach locally, and care for Marilla. Following the death of Thomas Lynde, Marilla invited the widowed Rachel Lynde to move into Green Gables, a living arrangement that ultimately freed Anne to leave her local teaching post and attend Redmond College.

value: Marilla Cuthbert said: “There, there, Marilla, you can have your own way,” said Matthew reassuringly. “Only be as good and kind to her as you can without spoiling her. I kind of think she’s one of the sort you can do anything with if you only get her to love you.”

value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "Matthew Cuthbert, I’m astonished at you. You know that Anne’s behavior was dreadful, and yet you take her part! I suppose you’ll be saying next thing that she oughtn’t to be punished at all!"

value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "She’ll have her meals regular, and I’ll carry them up to her myself. But she’ll stay up there until she’s willing to apologize to Mrs. Lynde, and that’s final, Matthew."

value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "and I can’t prevent her, for her father aids and abets her. She’s always poring over a book. I’m glad she has the prospect of a playmate—perhaps it will take her more out-of-doors."

value: Matthew Cuthbert is extremely shy.
unit: Extremely shy and unobservant, Matthew Cuthbert naturally avoids excitement and hates being among strangers, harboring a deep dread of women and little girls. He is an exceptionally quiet, patient, and hardworking man who rarely speaks or volunteers information, though he is a sympathetic and admiring listener to talkative people. Despite his difficulty with verbal arguments, he displays an amazing silent persistency when holding onto his opinions. Known for his good-natured and kind disposition, he is deeply indulgent and holds a strong sympathy toward Anne.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert lived at Green Gables.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert, an extremely shy man who lived at Green Gables, had worn a full soft brown beard since age twenty and generally dreaded all women except his sister Marilla and Mrs. Rachel Lynde. Despite his usual reluctance to leave home, he drove to Bright River station expecting to collect an orphan boy to help on the farm, only to find a talkative young girl named Anne Shirley instead. Although Marilla initially wanted to return the child, Matthew gently advocated for keeping her. He grew deeply fond of Anne, secretly persuading her to apologize to Mrs. Lynde after a quarrel, bringing her sweeties, and giving her a calf he bought from Mr. Bell. He consistently encouraged her pursuits, convincing Marilla to let her attend a local concert and later enduring an embarrassing attempt at a store before enlisting Mrs. Lynde's help to procure a stylish brown dress with puffed sleeves for Anne's Christmas gift. As Anne matured and succeeded academically, Matthew proudly shared in her achievements, including her entrance into Queen's Academy and her winning of the Avery Scholarship. Following her return home from academy commencement, Anne noticed his failing health during a memorable evening walk. Shortly thereafter, Matthew collapsed and died suddenly upon reading news of a bank failure.

label: History
value: Paul Irving is an imaginative student.
unit: Paul Irving is an imaginative student at the Avonlea school who lost his mother three years prior. On Anne Shirley's first day of teaching, Paul cheers her up by giving her wild orchids, and he later writes a composition detailing his fantastical adventures with imaginary friends. Over time, he continues to bond with Anne, sharing his thoughts about his parents, rock people, and childhood worries, which causes some jealousy in Davy. When news spreads that Anne is resigning her teaching post to attend college, Paul is deeply distressed. During a visit to Echo Lodge, Paul connects with Miss Lavendar over their shared experiences with imaginary dream-people, paving the way for his returning father, Stephen Irving, to reunite with and marry her. Following the wedding, Paul expresses excitement about moving to Boston.

value: Phillips is a local schoolteacher.
unit: As a local schoolteacher who boarded at Eben Wright's house, Phillips was known for frequently whipping his students and maintaining poor order in his classroom. When Gilbert Blythe teased Anne Shirley, prompting her to smash her slate over Gilbert's head, Phillips punished Anne by making her stand at the blackboard. Later, Phillips publicly disciplined Anne for being late by forcing her to sit next to Gilbert, an act that drove Anne to temporarily quit attending his school.

label: Personality
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde is a remarkably capable person.
unit: A remarkably capable person, Mrs. Rachel Lynde manages her own affairs as well as those of others, maintaining a busybody presence while keeping a sharp, observant eye on everything that passes. Known as a red-hot politician, an active church worker, and a skilled sewer, she prides herself on being outspoken and always speaking her mind without fear or favor. Though her somewhat officious nature can lead her to be critical and easily shocked by any naughtiness, she remains at heart a kind, good soul who dearly loves to give advice. She considers herself a pretty good judge of human nature, though she holds pessimistic views about the world and firmly believes in foreordination. Endowed with strong, long-lasting opinions, she is notably farseeing, highly curious, and strongly opposed to higher education for women.

unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde had brought up ten children and buried two, knitted sixteen cotton warp quilts, and lived as neighbors with Marilla Cuthbert for forty-five years without a quarrel. Following Matthew's sudden death, Rachel praised Anne's growth, and she shared in the community's grief. As the years passed, Rachel kept up with local news, regularly exchanging gossip with Marilla and Anne about upcoming village events, town improvements, and new residents. When her husband Thomas Lynde died, Marilla invited Rachel to move into Green Gables so she would not have to leave Avonlea, an arrangement that enabled Anne to step down from her teaching job to attend college.

label: History
value: Shirley resigned from her position as the Avonlea schoolteacher
unit: Shirley resigned from her position as the Avonlea schoolteacher to attend Redmond College after Rachel Lynde moved in to keep Marilla company. During her summer vacation, she spent time visiting Echo Lodge with her student Paul Irving, where she noticed the despondency of Miss Lavendar. Shirley helped facilitate a reconciliation between Miss Lavendar and Paul's returning father, Stephen Irving, by delivering a message and helping prepare for his arrival. After assisting with the preparations, she attended their intimate garden wedding and shared a quiet, meaningful moment with Gilbert Blythe before leaving Echo Lodge.

label: Quote
value: Shirley said: "In the years to come thy memory will shine like a star over my lonely life, as that last story we read together says. Diana, wilt thou give me a lock of thy jet-black tresses in parting to treasure forevermore?"

label: Quote
value: Shirley said: "Fare thee well, my beloved friend. Henceforth we must be as strangers though living side by side. But my heart will ever be faithful to thee."

label: Quote
value: Shirley said: "That is all there is left in life for me, now that my friend has been ruthlessly torn from me. In school I can look at her and muse over days departed."

label: Quote
value: Shirley said: “I think he has only been its nominal head for many years,” said Anne. “He is a very old man; his nephews are really at the head of the institution.”

label: Quote
value: Shirley said: “If I had been the boy you sent for,” said Anne wistfully, “I’d be able to help you so much now and spare you in a hundred ways. I could find it in my heart to wish I had been, just for that.”

value: Anne is in a bad mood from a toothache.

unit: In a bad mood from a toothache, Anne accidentally causes fireworks to explode in the schoolroom and subsequently whips Anthony Pye after he puts a mouse in her desk. She goes home heartbroken over her bad day, but Marilla comforts her. The next morning, Anthony treats Anne with new respect, and Mrs. Rachel Lynde later confirms that the whipping gained his approval.

chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans on their drive home from Carmody when they spot a Jersey cow trampling Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing the cow is her own nuisance Jersey, Dolly, Anne impulsively sells the stray cow on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.

unit: A massive hail and thunder storm strikes Avonlea on the exact day predicted in a lighthearted newspaper note, causing severe damage across the village. Later, Gilbert visits Green Gables to discuss the storm's destruction and note the destruction of an old blighted house.

value: Marilla returns home to Green Gables.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXVII. Vanity and Vexation of Spirit
unit: Marilla returns home to Green Gables expecting supper, but finds the stove unlit and Anne nowhere in sight. When Marilla goes upstairs, she discovers Anne hiding under her pillows because she dyed her red hair green using hair dye bought from a peddler. After washing fails to remove the green color, Marilla cuts Anne's hair off short, leaving Anne to reflect remorsefully on her vanity.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid
unit: Anne and her friends re-enact a poem on a flat-bottomed boat, but the boat begins to leak, stranding Anne on a bridge pile. After returning home safely, Anne reflects on learning another lesson, while Matthew quietly encourages her not to abandon all her romance.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road
unit: Marilla learns from an oculist that she must give up heavy eye work or face total blindness, putting the future of Green Gables in jeopardy. Anne decides to forfeit her college scholarship, stay at home to care for Marilla, and take up a local teaching job instead. After learning Gilbert Blythe gave up the Avonlea school so she could have it, Anne meets Gilbert on her way home and they finally end their feud to become close friends.

chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans on their drive home from Carmody when they spot a Jersey cow trampling Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing the cow is her own nuisance Jersey, Dolly, Anne impulsively sells the stray cow on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.

When Marilla goes upstairs, she discovers Anne hiding under her pillows because she dyed her red hair green using hair dye bought from a peddler. After washing fails to remove the green color, Marilla cuts Anne's hair off short, leaving Anne to reflect remorsefully on her vanity.

chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans on their drive home from Carmody when they spot a Jersey cow trampling Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing the cow is her own nuisance Jersey, Dolly, Anne impulsively sells the stray cow on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.
